text: Revised position on the protected-base choice after reading the eight call sites. A local protected base is not a small addition: protectedBranchRef returns refs/remotes/origin/<branch> and is consumed by propose, archive eligibility, archive pull-request publication, maintainer attestation, and the protected-base initialization production. Archive publication and attestation are about a published base by definition, so a local mode leaves their meaning undefined rather than merely unimplemented. The engine refusing to plan against a base that does not exist, and converting that refusal into a Fail-Grant challenge that asks a person to create it, is the correct behaviour under R-000: it is one authorized action, not a workaround. What was actually missing was that `now` and `finding convert --now` surfaced the raw error instead of the challenge, which is fixed. Recommend closing this item and, if a local-only protected base is still wanted, opening it as a design change that states what archive and attestation mean without a remote.
